name: CineStill 50D
notes: CineStill publishes no technical data. CineStill 50D is reported to be Kodak Vision3 50D (5203) with its rem-jet anti-halation backing removed, processed in C-41; this look is the 5203 datasheet curves printed on a colour paper.
The red glow around highlights (halation) is modelled; its radius, threshold and strength are Grainy's choice, not published values.

Read from the November 2011 Spanish vector copy (H-1-5203t, kodak-vision3-50d-2011-es.pdf; title 'KODAK VISION3 50D 5203/7203', printer's proof with crop marks). The current English copy (H-1-5203, revised 3-26, kodak-vision3-50d.pdf) has the same plots as raster images; its spectral-sensitivity plot has y axis labels (4.0 ... 0.0) that do not line up with its grid lines, so the Spanish vector copy was used. Labels in the Spanish copy: Curvas sensitometricas, Curvas de sensibilidad espectral, Curvas de la densidad espectral de los colorantes.

Exposure indexes printed: daylight (5500 K) 50 with no filter; tungsten (3000 K or 3200 K) 12 with the Wratten 2 / 80A filter. The curves are for 5500 K daylight, 1/50 s, so balance is daylight and iso 50.

Characteristic curves: the top axis (log exposure, lux-seconds) is printed with only three labels: -3.03 at the left frame, -0.515 in the middle and 2.006 at the right frame; the bottom axis gives camera stops -8 to +8 over the same width (stop 0 = log -0.515). x is the printed log exposure read from those labels (5.04 log units wide). The red (r) curve is drawn dotted on this sheet, so its trace relies on the curve's vector path (strict hints) rather than on continuous ink. Densitometry: Status M.
No Log H Ref or grey-card density table is printed, so log_h_ref is null.

Spectral sensitivity: effective exposure 1/10 s (as printed), ECN-2, Status M, density 0.2 above D-min; y is log sensitivity (reciprocal exposure in erg/cm2) as printed, the layers peak at about 1.6 to 1.8 (a far lower level than the 200T and 500T sheets). The yellow-forming layer (b) is drawn from about 360 to 500 nm, magenta (g) 480 to 595 nm, cyan (r) 575 to 680 nm, and each curve ends on the 0.0 axis line.

Spectral dye density: ECN-2, D-mins subtracted, diffuse density; the plot ends at 760 nm (no data from 760 to 800 nm), unlike the 200T and 500T sheets. The cyan, magenta and yellow curves are peak-normalised (peak 1.0), mid is the Midscale Neutral curve (Escala media neutra), min the dashed Minimum Density curve (Densidad minima).

Grain: the sheet gives diffuse rms granularity curves only (48 micrometre aperture, ECN-2; Sigma D scale on the right, multiply by 1000), no single printed value, so grain is null. Read by eye, Sigma D is roughly 0.003 to 0.006 for the green and red records (rms about 3 to 6) and 0.006 to 0.010 for the blue record, depending on density.
Print film: none is named on the sheet; LAD values are said to be specific to each print or duplicating film.
